dsh-jev-guard assesses bash and pwsh commands before DSH executes them. It uses local rules, a fast prefilter, or Jev, then returns an allow, ask, or deny decision. It also tracks retries and writes audit records. Jev assessment requires a TypeSafe API key.

dsh-jev-guard 的功能「静态规则与快速筛查」：命令先经过静态规则和预筛路径；符合规则时可直接返回结果，其他情况继续后续评估流程。
dsh-jev-guard 的功能「脚本上下文补充」：对可识别的脚本调用读取有限长度的脚本正文并补充到判定状态，供服务端评估使用。
dsh-jev-guard 的功能「审计记录」：将命令判定的动作、来源和相关字段按 JSONL 追加到本地日志，并对日志大小进行轮转处理。

|---|---|---|
| `allow` | Provably read-only, or judged safe | Run it |
| `revise` | Not enough evidence to run safely, but a better form very likely exists | The **model** rewrites and retries (three downgrade templates: dry run first / narrow the scope / back up first) |
| `block` | Would irreversibly delete or overwrite, or hit a hard rule | Refused; a human runs it by hand |

dsh-jev-guard README · What it does：1. **L0 static hard rules** (`lib/rules.js`): 26 "never allowed" + 24 "human confirmation required". **Offline and impossible to override** — not even a one-shot token gets past them. Rules match at **command position only** (the start of a line, or after `;` `&` `|` `(` `$(`, or after `bash -c "` / `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "` / `cmd /c "`, and skipping wrappers such as `sudo` / `timeout 30` / `xargs -0` / `find … -exec`) — so *mentioning* a dangerous command inside an argument is not a false positive, **and a real command buried in a multi-line script is not missed either**. Only two rules cannot be anchored structurally (`redirect-to-device`, `fork-bomb`) and match the whole text; the counter `RULE_STATS.anywhere` is always 2.
2. **Pre-screen**: commands that are provably read-only or touch only rebuildable content (caches, build output, `/tmp`) pass straight through, with **zero network calls**.
3. **Jev semantic judgment**: one yes/no question — *"will this command irreversibly delete or overwrite the user's real data?"* — split by two thresholds into `allow` / `revise` / `block`. Measured latency ~300ms (P50 267ms), cost ≈ `$0.000019` per c

dsh-jev-guard README · 3. Restart DSH (plugins are not hot-reloaded)：`cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin on `tools/pre-execute`, and **every tunable lives there** (you can also put them in `config.json`, which lives **outside the package** — `~/.jev-guard/config.json`, or wherever `JEV_GUARD_CONFIG` points; precedence is `patch > config.json > built-in defaults`).

dsh-jev-guard README · 3. Restart DSH (plugins are not hot-reloaded)：**API key** — three sources, highest precedence first: the DSH credentials layer (`ctx.credentials`, rotation needs no restart) → the environment variable `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` → a `secrets.json` **you create yourself** (default `~/.jev-guard/secrets.json`, `{"TYPESAFE_API_KEY": "apikey_..."}`). That file is deliberately **not** part of the repository or of the published package, so nobody ships one to you — the two sources above it are the ones to prefer. Keeping it outside the package is what makes it survive an update: `npm i` / `dsh plugin update` replaces the whole package directory, so a copy inside it would be wiped. `node bin/guard.mjs key set` writes that file for you (mode 0600), and the DSH adapter reads it too. The key is never printed, and it is masked before anything is written to the log.bash
node bin/guard.mjs selftest      # expect: all 12 checks pass (offline)
node bin/guard.mjs status        # expect: ✅ healthy (exit code 3 while degraded)
```

dsh-jev-guard README · 3. Restart DSH (plugins are not hot-reloaded)：Then run a command in a session that is **certain** to be blocked (e.g. `git push --force origin main`): it should be refused, and that record should appear in `node bin/guard.mjs log --tail 3`.

|---|---|---|
| `revise` (50–70%) | **Handed to a human approval prompt** | Refused **+ downgrade templates + one-shot token hint** |

text: dsh-jev-guard README · Behavior under the two approval policies：> **Why `ask` mode hands both the grey zone and the high scores to a human**: when a person is right there, letting a 50.6% judgment decide for them makes no sense; and under `never` there is nobody to ask, so the valve can only refuse conservatively. When the host has no responder, approval is **fail-closed**, so handing something to a human does **not** turn into automatic approval while unattended; the prompt only ever offers `allowed-once`, never a lasting bypass.
section: Behavior under the two approval policies

text: dsh-jev-guard README · Behavior under the two approval policies：> **L0 `deny`-class hard rules are an absolute gate**: they block under both policies, and even `retryLimit`'s "retry enough and a human handles it" does not apply to them — otherwise one click on "allow" in a prompt would bypass the hard floor (a token cannot cross L0, and neither can an approval).

text: dsh-jev-guard README · Behavior under the two approval policies：> `danger-full-access` = `{ sandbox: 'danger-full-access', approval: 'never' }` — **no sandbox underneath, approval effectively off: the valve is the only layer left**. That is exactly why it exists, and it is also the situation where a wrong verdict costs the most. Audit records carry the sandbox preset (`preset`) and the approval policy (`policy`) for that call, so a retrospective can tell whether a sandbox was still behind it at the time.

section: When credit runs out: degrade, don't fail silently

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · When credit runs out: degrade, don't fail silently：| Situation | What the valve does | Where you see it |
|---|---|---|
| Credit exhausted / key invalid (`402` / `401`) | **Degrades**: writes `~/.jev-guard/degraded.json` and stops sending requests for the cooldown window (to save money), running only the **free L0 + pre-screen** by default | `guard status` (exit code 3) · one `⚠️` line in the refusal reason · `source: degraded` and `level: warn` in the audit · stderr of the CLI |
| Cooldown expires | Automatically sends **one** probe request: success restores normal operation (you do nothing), failure keeps it degraded | `guard status` shows how long is left |
| This egress is outside the service's region (`451`, carrying the service's own JSON body) | **Degrades for 30 minutes, globally** — the request reached the service and was refused by its region policy, and every entry point on this machine shares one egress | `guard status` names the cause (exit code 3) · the warning says to check the proxy and the egress IP · `errorKind: region` in `guard log --stats` |
| The request itself is refused (`400` / `422`, e.g. `Unknown model: …`) | **Degrades for 15 minut
section: When credit runs out: degrade, don't fail silently

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · When credit runs out: degrade, don't fail silently：```bash
node bin/guard.mjs status --clear    # don't want to wait out the cooldown: retry once now (a failure re-enters degradation)
```

If you want "once the credit is gone, don't interfere at all" (L0 included), set `degradePolicy: "off"`.
section: When credit runs out: degrade, don't fail silently

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · If the service refuses your region: the region lock：The judging service is **not reachable from every region**: a request sent from a blocked egress comes back `HTTP 451` with
the service's own body, `{"title":"Typesafe is not available in your region.","status":451}` — refused before
authentication and before the body is validated. Measured on 2026-10-15 through the production path: the **same request
body** returns `422` (a body-validation error, i.e. it arrived) from an allowed egress and `451` from a blocked one.
section: If the service refuses your region: the region lock

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · If the service refuses your region: the region lock：- **It is not a plugin fault, and not a key problem.** The key is never checked; a fresh, valid key fails identically.
- **It is a property of the egress, shared by every entry point on the machine** — the DSH host process, the CLI, a
  scheduled job — which is why the `region` class degrades **globally** for 30 minutes instead of per entry point.
- **It is loud now.** Before 0.5.5 the whole condition was classified `unknown`, and `unknown` degrades nothing: the valve
  failed open on every command, kept re-sending requests the service had just refused (83 in one measured session, all
  `source: error`), and `guard status` still printed "normal". Now `guard status` names the cause and the warning tells you
  to check the proxy and the egress IP.
section: If the service refuses your region: the region lock

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · If the service refuses your region: the region lock：**How to run in a blocked region:** route the **DSH host process** through an egress in an allowed region. What bites on
Windows is that this routing is often applied **per executable**: a proxy configured only for your shell leaves
`DeepSeek Harness.exe` going out directly — measured here on 2026-10-15, a proxied shell resolved to a US exit while the
host binary, running the *same* script, resolved to a Chinese one and got `451`. Verify from inside the host rather than
from a terminal: `node bin/guard.mjs judge 'ls'` should come back `source: jev`, and `guard log --stats` should show no
`region` count.
section: If the service refuses your region: the region lock

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · If the service refuses your region: the region lock：**The honest limit:** the valve cannot fix your egress. Under a region lock its job is to stop spending requests it has
been told will be refused, and to say so instead of reporting health for a session in which nothing was judged. The
`region` cooldown probes once per 30 minutes, so it recovers by itself as soon as the egress changes — see
[`docs/DECISIONS.md`](./docs/DECISIONS.md) D17.

dsh-jev-guard README · Security and privacy：1. **The only things sent to the judging service are the command text and, optionally, script bodies** (sensitive paths — `.env` / `.ssh` / `*.pem` / `*credential*` / `*secret*` / `*token*` — are skipped automatically, with an 8KB per-file cap). To turn this off entirely: `inlineScripts: false` (at the cost of `node x.mjs`-style commands dropping back into the p≈0.31 blind spot).
2. **The key is read only from the credentials layer / environment / `secrets.json`** and never enters the log or a report (the command text is masked before writing).
3. **Every failure is fail-open**: when the judging service is unavailable nothing is blocked — DSH's own sandbox preset (anything except `danger-full-access`) still applies before execution. If you want "block even when the service is down", thicken the L0 rules rather than switching to fail-closed.
4. **It does not defend against deliberate bypass**: rewriting the command, encoding it, or writing the authorisation file directly can all get around it. Defending against malicious injection takes a sandbox / a low-privilege user / a container.

dsh-jev-guard README · Known limits：**It is an accident net, not a security boundary.** It guards against *accidents* — a mistyped command, an opaque script, the moment nobody stops when full access is granted; it does **not** guard against an *adversary*. This is not unfinished work but an explicit decision: the known and deliberately kept bypasses, together with "under what circumstances to reconsider", are written up in **D1** of [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) — **please do not "helpfully" seal them.**

dsh-jev-guard README · Known limits：Two more deliberate omissions: judging **does not simulate filesystem state** (it will not reason "that file is empty anyway"), and it does not accept "this command is harmless" arguments that would require reading runtime state — that is precisely the crack accidents come in through.

dsh-jev-guard README · dsh-jev-guard：> **英文摘要** — `dsh-jev-guard` is a pre-execution safety valve for DeepSeek Harness. It judges every `bash` / `pwsh` tool call **before** it runs — offline static rules first, then a paid semantic model — and returns one of four states (`allow` / `revise` / `block` / `escalate`). It blocks unrecoverable commands, teaches the model a safer form when it can, offers a one-shot human token when neither is right, and **degrades loudly instead of silently** when the judging API runs out of credit. **It is an accident net, not a security boundary** — see [已知边界](#已知边界).

|---|---|---|
| `allow` | 确定性只读,或判定为安全 | 直接执行 |
| `revise` | 证据不足以安全执行,但很可能有更好的写法 | **模型**换写法重试(附三种降级模板:先演练 / 缩小范围 / 先备份) |
| `block` | 会不可逆地删或覆盖,或命中硬规则 | 拒绝;由人手动执行 |

dsh-jev-guard README · 它做什么：1. **L0 静态硬规则**(`lib/rules.js`):26 条"永不允许" + 24 条"必须人工确认"。**不联网、不可被覆盖**,连一次性令牌也过不去。规则只在**命令位置**匹配(每一行行首,或 `;` `&` `|` `(` `$(` 之后,或 `bash -c "` / `pwsh -NoProfile -Command "` / `cmd /c "` 之后,并允许 `sudo`/`timeout 30`/`xargs -0`/`find … -exec` 这类包装器)—— 所以"在参数里提到危险命令"不会被误伤,**而多行脚本里的真命令也不会被漏掉**。只有两条结构上锚不了的规则(`redirect-to-device`、`fork-bomb`)是全文匹配,计数器 `RULE_STATS.anywhere` 恒为 2。
2. **预筛**:可证明只读或只影响可重建内容(缓存、构建产物、`/tmp`)的命令直接放行,**零网络调用**。
3. **Jev 语义判定**:一次是非问句 —— *"这条命令会不可逆地删除或覆盖用户的真实数据吗?"* —— 按两个阈值切成 `allow` / `revise` / `block`。实测延迟 ~300ms(P50 267ms),成本 ≈ `$0.000019`/次。

section: 两种审批策略下的行为

text:
dsh-jev-guard README · 两种审批策略下的行为：> **为什么 `ask` 模式下灰区和高分都交给人**:人就在场时,让一个 50.6% 的判断替人做决定没有道理;而 `never` 模式下没人可问,只能由阀门保守地拒。宿主没有应答者时审批是 **fail-closed**,所以转人工**不会**在无人值守时变成自动放行;弹窗只给 `allowed-once`,不留长期旁路。
>
> **L0 的 `deny` 类硬规则是绝对闸门**:两种模式都拦死,连 `retryLimit` 的"反复重试就交人"也不适用于它 —— 否则弹窗里点一次"允许"就绕过了硬地板(令牌不能越过 L0,审批同样不能)。

> `danger-full-access` = `{ sandbox: 'danger-full-access', approval: 'never' }` —— **没有沙箱兜底、审批也等于关掉,阀门是唯一一层**。这正是它存在的意义,也是它判错时代价最大的场景。审计记录里会带上当次的沙箱档位(`preset`)与审批策略(`policy`),事后复盘能看出"当时后面还有没有沙箱"。

四条性质:**绑定命令原文**(换一个字就是另一个令牌)、**用掉即删**(无法重放)、**不越过 L0 硬规则**、**只在交互终端授权**(AI 自己跑会被拒)。

**② DSH 审批弹窗(`approval: ask`)。** 阀门只负责把命令标成"需要人看",由 DSH 弹框;弹窗里的理由就是阀门原文。DSH 的答案是闭集(只有"允许一次"和"拒绝"),所以**每次都是一次独立的逐次决定**,没有"永久允许"可以被静默吞掉。

**③ 人直接执行。** 你在自己终端里跑那条命令 —— 阀门不参与,也**不会因此给 AI 任何权限**:审计里不会有你那次动作的记录,AI 重试同一条命令仍然会被拦。

dsh-jev-guard README · 服务拒绝你的地区时:地区锁：- **不是插件故障,也不是密钥问题。** 密钥根本没被检查过;换一把全新的、有效的密钥,结果一模一样。

  fail-open、把服务刚刚拒过的请求一遍遍再发出去(实测一场会话 83 条,全是 `source: error`),而 `guard status`
  一直打印"正常"。现在 `guard status` 会点名原因,告警会告诉你去查代理与出口 IP。

dsh-jev-guard README · 服务拒绝你的地区时:地区锁：**在被拦的地区怎么跑起来:** 让 **DSH 宿主进程**走一个允许地区的出口。Windows 上坑人的地方在于:这种分流往往是**按
可执行文件**生效的 —— 只给你的终端配了代理,`DeepSeek Harness.exe` 仍然直连出网:本机 2026-10-15 实测,同一份脚本
在配好代理的终端里拿到了美国出口,而由宿主二进制运行时拿到的是中国出口,于是吃了 `451`。验证要在宿主内部做、不是
在终端里做:`node bin/guard.mjs judge 'ls'` 应当回 `source: jev`,而 `guard log --stats` 里不该有 `region` 计数。

**诚实的上限:** 阀门修不了你的出口。地区锁之下它的职责是:不再花请求去撞一扇已经被告知会关的门,并且**说出来**,

dsh-jev-guard README · 安全与隐私：1. **会发给判定服务的只有命令文本 + 可选脚本正文**(敏感路径 `.env` / `.ssh` / `*.pem` / `*credential*` / `*secret*` / `*token*` 自动跳过,单文件 8KB 上限)。想彻底关闭:`inlineScripts: false`(代价是 `node x.mjs` 这类命令退回 p≈0.31 的盲区)。
2. **密钥只从凭据层 / 环境变量 / `secrets.json` 读取**,不进日志、不进报告(命令文本写入前掩码)。
3. **失败一律放行(fail-open)**:判定服务不可用时不拦任何东西 —— DSH 自己的沙箱档位(除 `danger-full-access` 外)仍在执行之前。想"服务挂了也拦",加厚 L0 规则,而不是改成 fail-closed。
4. **不防蓄意绕过**:换写法、编码、直接写授权文件都可能绕开。防恶意注入要靠沙箱 / 低权限用户 / 容器。

dsh-jev-guard README · 已知边界：**它是事故安全网,不是安全边界。** 它防的是*事故* —— 写错的命令、不透明的脚本、完全权限下没人拦的那一下;它**不**防*对手*。这不是没做完,是显式决策:已知且有意保留的旁路、以及"什么情况下该重新考虑",都写在 [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) 的 **D1**,**请不要"顺手把它堵上"**。

同样刻意的两条:判定**不模拟文件系统状态**(不会推理"反正那个文件已经是空的"),也不接受"这条命令没害处"这类需要读运行时状态的辩解 —— 那正是事故钻进来的缝。
